## Bottom line
- **The premise needs correcting.** IEEE 1588 PTP and Scheduled Action Commands were added in **GigE Vision 2.0 (Nov 2011)**, not 3.0. GigE Vision 2.1 (Aug 2018) then added an "updated profile for IEEE1588".
- **GigE Vision 3.0 adds RDMA streaming.** The GigE Vision Technical Committee approved it on 17 Apr 2026 and A3 announced the release on 12–13 May 2026. It adds RDMA over RoCEv2 through a new **GVRSP** streaming protocol, and a larger control-channel packet size. None of the A3 3.0 pages I read (the press release, FAQ, standard page and Industry Insight article) mention PTP, IEEE 1588 or time sync.
- **"Single cable" is PoE plus PTP plus scheduled action commands.** PoE comes from IEEE 802.3af/at, a separate standard from GigE Vision.

## Timeline
Sources: the [A3 GigE Vision standard page](https://www.automate.org/vision/vision-standards/vision-standards-gige-vision) plus the dated press releases linked below.
- **1.0, May 2006.** Covers discovery, GVCP (control), GVSP (streaming) and the GenICam XML description ([A3 2006 press release](https://www.automate.org/news/gige-vision-interface-standard-has-strong-european-debut-at-vision-2006), [Control Design](https://www.controldesign.com/articles/2007/016)).
- **1.1, announced 23 Apr 2009.** Added new pixel and Bayer formats, better error handling, and "action commands … to multiple devices simultaneously as well as managing the execution time" ([A3 press release](https://www.automate.org/news/gige-vision-version-1-1-interface-standard-released)).
- **1.2, Jan 2010.** Added control of non-streaming devices ([A3 press release](https://www.automate.org/vision/news/gige-vision-camera-interface-standard-version-1-2-released)).
- **2.0, Nov 2011.** Added 10GigE, link aggregation, compressed images (JPEG, JPEG 2000, H.264), multi-camera sync and multi-tap sensor support. The EMVA SFNC change history (the GenICam standard feature names document) lists for 2.0: IEEE 1588, unconditional and scheduled action commands, the ActionLate event, PAUSE frames and extended IDs ([SFNC 2.8 PDF](https://www.emva.org/wp-content/uploads/GenICam_SFNC_v2_8.pdf), pp. 29-30). The Wireshark dissectors mark these as "2.0 support" ([packet-gvcp.c L416-L482](https://github.com/wireshark/wireshark/blob/98a6cfdba1ab23f3c835b17df802004bc9429040/epan/dissectors/packet-gvcp.c#L416-L482)). Payload types JPEG 0x6, JPEG2000 0x7 and H264 0x8 are marked "GEV 2.0" ([packet-gvsp.c L43-L54](https://github.com/wireshark/wireshark/blob/98a6cfdba1ab23f3c835b17df802004bc9429040/epan/dissectors/packet-gvsp.c#L43-L54)).
- **2.1, Aug 2018.** Added multi-part payload (0xA) and the updated IEEE1588 profile. New registers list the supported profiles (bits for a "PTP profile" and an "802.1AS profile") and the selected profile ([packet-gvcp.c L3380-L3398](https://github.com/wireshark/wireshark/blob/98a6cfdba1ab23f3c835b17df802004bc9429040/epan/dissectors/packet-gvcp.c#L3380-L3398)). The IEEE 1588 profile registry lists "GigE Vision 2.1" as a PTP profile document ([IEEE SA](https://sagroups.ieee.org/1588/ptp-profiles)).
- **2.2, Jun 2022.** Added GenDC streaming (payload 0xB), multi-event data, and deprecated MultiZone.
- **3.0, 2026.** Adds RoCEv2 and GVRSP as a supplement to GVSP v2. It drops legacy GVSP v1, RDMA is optional, and it needs a RoCEv2 NIC and a GVRSP-capable library ([A3 FAQ](https://www.automate.org/vision/blogs/gige-vision-3-0-standard-answers-to-frequently-asked-questions-faq), [A3 press release](https://www.automate.org/vision/news/a3-officially-releases-gige-vision-3-0-opening-new-possibilities-in-machine-vision)). GVCP is kept for discovery and configuration ([A3 RoCEv2 page](https://www.automate.org/vision/vision-standards/rocev2-integration-into-gige-vision-standard-a-leap-forward-in-imaging-technology)).

## PTP edition
- SFNC 2.8 (dated 2026-04-08) tells readers to "Refer to the IEEE 1588-2008 specification" for PtpStatus.
- Basler's PTP documentation says "IEEE 1588-2008, also known as PTP Version 2" ([Basler docs](https://docs.baslerweb.com/precision-time-protocol)).
- I found no source linking any GigE Vision version to IEEE 1588-2019.

## How a host tells which version a camera implements
- **Version register at 0x0000:** major version in the upper 16 bits, minor in the lower 16. It is also the first field of the DISCOVERY_ACK reply, so you can read it during discovery.
- **GVCP Capability register at 0x0934** (big-endian masks, from the Wireshark hf definitions at [L3468-L3502](https://github.com/wireshark/wireshark/blob/98a6cfdba1ab23f3c835b17df802004bc9429040/epan/dissectors/packet-gvcp.c#L3468-L3502)):
  - 0x00080000: IEEE1588
  - 0x00020000: Scheduled Action
  - 0x00100000: Unconditional Action
  - 0x00010000: IEEE1588 extended capabilities (2.1)
  - 0x00000040: Action
- **Other registers:**
  - 0x0954 bit 0x00080000: enables 1588
  - 0x096C: 1588 status
  - 0x0970: scheduled-action queue size
  - 0x0974 to 0x097C: profile registers (2.1)
  - 0x090C: action device key
  - 0x9800 + 0x10·n: action group key/mask n
- **ACTION_CMD** is command 0x0100. When header flag 0x80 is set it carries a 64-bit scheduled time ([L2092-L2114](https://github.com/wireshark/wireshark/blob/98a6cfdba1ab23f3c835b17df802004bc9429040/epan/dissectors/packet-gvcp.c#L2092-L2114)).
- **Aravis** (main @482547a3, 2026-10-22; latest release 0.8.36 from 2026-04-26) defines only a subset of the capability bits. It has no host-side ACTION_CMD and no PTP register code ([arvgvcpprivate.h L95-L113 and L267-L282](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/blob/482547a3d56e3aa8d22d7ffed33c9f1588bfe17a/src/arvgvcpprivate.h#L267-L282)).
- **RDMA/GVRSP:** neither Aravis nor Wireshark has any RDMA, RoCE or GVRSP code.

## Test I ran
I wrote a stdlib-only raw GVCP register-read probe (`probe.py`) and ran it in `ubuntu:24.04` against `arv-fake-gv-camera-0.8` (aravis 0.8.30) over loopback.
- **Stock fake camera:** Version=0 and Capability=0. The emulator doesn't fill these registers in, so **it cannot emulate PTP or scheduled actions**.
- **With test values written in:** I wrote 0x00020001 into 0x0000 and 0x001B0067 into 0x0934 with `arv-tool`. The probe then decoded "2.1" plus IEEE1588, ScheduledAction, UnconditionalAction and the other set bits. That confirms the read-and-decode path works end to end.
- **On a real camera:** `python3 -I probe.py <camera-ip>` reports its real version and capabilities.
- Exact commands and outputs are in `RUN.txt`.

Is there a sourced figure for real PTP sync accuracy over a PoE switch? Vendors give only network-dependent statements. The roughly 9 µs spread across 7 cameras in LUCID's sample output is my own calculation from their printed timestamps, not a figure they state.

## Aravis as SkellyCam's GigE Vision backend

**What and status.** [Aravis](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis) is a GLib/GObject C library for GigE Vision and USB3 Vision. Its license is LGPL-2.1-or-later ([README#L25](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/blob/482547a3d56e3aa8d22d7ffed33c9f1588bfe17a/README.md#L25)).
- Latest stable release: **0.8.36** (tagged 2026-04-23, "Latest" on GitHub).
- Latest development release: **0.9.2** (pre-release). `main` is 0.9.3, which uses API version 0.10.
- It is actively maintained: the last commit was 2026-10-22 and there were 49 commits in the past year. Linux, macOS, MinGW and MSVC CI all passed on 2026-10-23.
- The README says the GV/U3V protocol code must not be based on A3 spec documents ([README#L57-L63](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/blob/482547a3d56e3aa8d22d7ffed33c9f1588bfe17a/README.md#L57-L63)).

**License and SkellyCam (AGPL-3.0).**
- LGPL-2.1 §3 allows conversion to GPLv2-or-later, which makes it compatible with AGPL-3 ([COPYING#L211-L221](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/blob/482547a3d56e3aa8d22d7ffed33c9f1588bfe17a/COPYING#L211-L221)).
- §6(b) covers distributing it as a separately replaceable shared library, for example in a PyInstaller onedir bundle ([COPYING#L271-L304](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/blob/482547a3d56e3aa8d22d7ffed33c9f1588bfe17a/COPYING#L271-L304)). The bundle also needs a notice and a copy of the license.

**Platforms and Python.**
- **Linux:** Ubuntu 24.04 ships 0.8.30, including the `gir1.2-aravis-0.8` typelib. There is a Linux-only AF_PACKET TPACKET_V3 ring-buffer receive path ([meson.build#L103-L119](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/blob/482547a3d56e3aa8d22d7ffed33c9f1588bfe17a/meson.build#L103-L119), [arvgvstream.c#L1240-L1265](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/blob/482547a3d56e3aa8d22d7ffed33c9f1588bfe17a/src/arvgvstream.c#L1240-L1265)). It needs `cap_net_raw` ([ethernet.md#L94-L103](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/blob/482547a3d56e3aa8d22d7ffed33c9f1588bfe17a/docs/reference/aravis/ethernet.md#L94-L103)).
- **macOS:** the Homebrew formula is 0.8.36, with arm64 and x86_64 bottles ([formula](https://github.com/Homebrew/homebrew-core/blob/62967b0a1e5adb912fde3b160b73aa696c12672e/Formula/a/aravis.rb)). Upstream macOS CI builds with `-Dintrospection=disabled` ([aravis-macos.yml#L30](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/blob/482547a3d56e3aa8d22d7ffed33c9f1588bfe17a/.github/workflows/aravis-macos.yml#L30)), so Python on macOS is not tested upstream.
- **Windows:** the docs point to MSYS2 packages and an MSVC/Conan build ([building.md#L93-L109](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/blob/482547a3d56e3aa8d22d7ffed33c9f1588bfe17a/docs/reference/aravis/building.md#L93-L109)).
  - The [MSYS2 package](https://packages.msys2.org/base/mingw-w64-aravis) is behind, at 0.8.33-4.
  - MSVC CI builds without introspection ([aravis-msvc-conan2.yml#L77](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/blob/482547a3d56e3aa8d22d7ffed33c9f1588bfe17a/.github/workflows/aravis-msvc-conan2.yml#L77)).
  - Windows has no packet socket.
  - Issue [#752](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/issues/752) is open and unresolved: about 20 MiB/s on Windows against about 90 MiB/s on Ubuntu with the same 4K camera. There are also firewall pitfalls ([#830](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/issues/830)).
- **Python packaging:** there is no PyPI or conda-forge Aravis (both return 404). PyGObject on PyPI is sdist-only in every release. Python access therefore means a system Python with distro, Homebrew or MSYS2 GI packages, or a custom ctypes/cffi binding over the C API that ships glib, libxml2 and Aravis shared libraries. **This is the biggest blocker for SkellyCam's pip/uv workflow.**

**API.**
- Discovery: `arv_update_device_list` and related calls ([arvsystem.h#L35-L53](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/blob/482547a3d56e3aa8d22d7ffed33c9f1588bfe17a/src/arvsystem.h#L35-L53)).
- Feature access by name ([arvdevice.h#L143-L179](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/blob/482547a3d56e3aa8d22d7ffed33c9f1588bfe17a/src/arvdevice.h#L143-L179)).
- Stream and buffer pool, GV packet size/delay, multipart, triggers and chunks ([arvcamera.h#L237-L288](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/blob/482547a3d56e3aa8d22d7ffed33c9f1588bfe17a/src/arvcamera.h#L237-L288)).
- Chunk parser, covered by a unit test that passed in my run ([tests/genicam.c#L1159-L1230](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/blob/482547a3d56e3aa8d22d7ffed33c9f1588bfe17a/tests/genicam.c#L1159-L1230)).
- Socket-buffer AUTO/FIXED setting.
- Packet resend: on by default, and forced off when the device lacks the capability ([arvgvdevice.c#L1904-L1905](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/blob/482547a3d56e3aa8d22d7ffed33c9f1588bfe17a/src/arvgvdevice.c#L1904-L1905)).

**Raw or compressed?** Uncompressed PFNC pixel data (Mono8/16, Bayer, RGB and so on). The JPEG, JPEG2000 and H264 payload types are explicitly marked "(not supported)" ([arvbuffer.h#L64-L92](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/blob/482547a3d56e3aa8d22d7ffed33c9f1588bfe17a/src/arvbuffer.h#L64-L92)).

**Timestamps and PTP.**
- `arv_buffer_get_timestamp` returns the camera's 64-bit timestamp from the GVSP leader packet, converted to nanoseconds with the bootstrap `TimestampTickFrequency`.
- `arv_buffer_get_system_timestamp` is the host `g_get_real_time()` taken when the leader packet arrives.
- If the tick frequency is 0, the device timestamp silently falls back to the host time ([arvgvstream.c#L460-L531](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/blob/482547a3d56e3aa8d22d7ffed33c9f1588bfe17a/src/arvgvstream.c#L460-L531), [arvbuffer.c#L379-L437](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/blob/482547a3d56e3aa8d22d7ffed33c9f1588bfe17a/src/arvbuffer.c#L379-L437)).
- **libaravis has no PTP code at all.** The only PTP mention is an unreleased GStreamer `add-reference-timestamp-meta` option ([gstaravis.c#L563-L567](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/blob/482547a3d56e3aa8d22d7ffed33c9f1588bfe17a/gst/gstaravis.c#L563-L567)).
- The maintainer's position is that you enable PTP through generic GenICam feature writes ([#258](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/issues/258)).
- **Action commands are not implemented.** GVCP has no ACTION_CMD ([arvgvcpprivate.h#L249-L282](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/blob/482547a3d56e3aa8d22d7ffed33c9f1588bfe17a/src/arvgvcpprivate.h#L249-L282)). Issue [#184](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/issues/184) has been open since 2018, and draft PR [#468](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/pull/468) has been stalled since 2021.

**Tests run (Docker, ubuntu:24.04, `--network none`).**
- **Distro 0.8.30 with PyGObject 3.48.2:** `arv-fake-gv-camera-0.8 -i 127.0.0.1` was found on discovery. The script `aravis_fake_camera_capture.py` grabbed 100/100 Mono8 512×512 frames (262144 bytes each) with a 1 GHz tick frequency, at 24.7 fps by default and 100.2 fps when set to 100 Hz.
  - At 100 Hz the device-timestamp interval std was 0.16 ms, while the host-receive std was about 10 ms.
  - The fake camera's "device" timestamp is just host time ([arvfakecamera.c#L795](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/blob/482547a3d56e3aa8d22d7ffed33c9f1588bfe17a/src/arvfakecamera.c#L795-L796)), so this only shows the plumbing works, not PTP accuracy.
  - `get_data()` copies the frame (0.026 ms per 256 KiB).
- **HEAD build from source:** all 10 meson tests passed, including the genicam/chunk test, the Python tests and the `fakegv` network test. `ARAVIS_HAS_PACKET_SOCKET` is 1, and the same Python script ran against the Aravis-0.10 typelib.
- **Pitfall found:** without network isolation, discovery picked up another fake camera with the same id on the Docker bridge, and acquisition failed with a write_register timeout. Open cameras by IP or serial, not by id.

**Rust.** [aravis-rs](https://github.com/robohouse-delft/aravis-rs) 0.11.1 (2025-02-10, BSD-2) is generated from GIR and binds the 0.8 API up to 0.8.31. It links the system Aravis dynamically, so it has the same native-dependency packaging problem.

**Verdict.** Viable as a **Linux-first, optional** backend. macOS is likely workable through Homebrew but untested here. Windows works, but it lags, has no packet socket, and has an open throughput issue. Across all three OSes it is **not** an easily pip-installable, equally performant backend, and it gives no help with PTP setup or action-command sync beyond raw timestamps and generic feature access.

result.summary_markdown:
## pyGigEVision (ladisk), evaluated at commit `2de2531` / v0.2.2

**Verdict: not suitable as SkellyCam's base. Useful as MIT-licensed reference code for GVCP/GVSP packet framing.**

### Facts
- MIT license, Python >=3.10. Its only dependencies are numpy and psutil ([pyproject.toml#L37-L40](https://github.com/ladisk/pyGigEVision/blob/2de253135b8766c1eb752226539a16b810a1cf0f/pyproject.toml#L37-L40)).
- It implements GVCP and GVSP itself in pure Python using `socket`. It does not use a vendor SDK, GenTL/Harvesters or Aravis.
- Created 2026-05-11. Last commit 2026-07-08. PyPI has 0.2.1 (2026-06-11) and 0.2.2 (2026-07-08).
- 6 stars. About 67 of 69 commits are by one author (Jaša Šonc, Univ. Ljubljana).
- Two open PRs from 2026-10-20: [#3](https://github.com/ladisk/pyGigEVision/pull/3) raises the 2048×2048 pixel cap, and [#4](https://github.com/ladisk/pyGigEVision/pull/4) works around the macOS firewall.
- CI runs on Ubuntu and Windows with Python 3.10–3.13. There is no macOS CI.
- The 85 unit tests are all mock-based ([conftest.py](https://github.com/ladisk/pyGigEVision/blob/2de253135b8766c1eb752226539a16b810a1cf0f/tests/conftest.py#L1-L2) says there are no hardware tests). I reran them: 85 passed.

### What it supports
- **Discovery:** across all network interfaces ([gvcp.py#L309-L423](https://github.com/ladisk/pyGigEVision/blob/2de253135b8766c1eb752226539a16b810a1cf0f/pyGigEVision/gvcp.py#L309-L423)), plus FORCEIP.
- **Control:** READREG, WRITEREG and READMEM, with retries and PENDING_ACK handling. CCP control and a heartbeat thread.
- **GenICam XML:** download only. It does **not** parse the XML or offer feature access by name ([genicam.py#L15-L19](https://github.com/ladisk/pyGigEVision/blob/2de253135b8766c1eb752226539a16b810a1cf0f/pyGigEVision/genicam.py#L15-L19)).
- **Streaming:** a GVSP receiver with one Python thread per stream and a `recvfrom` call per packet. It does packet resend.
- **Pixel formats:** only unpacked Mono8/10/12/14/16. Any other format defaults to 2 bytes per pixel ([gvsp.py#L55-L76](https://github.com/ladisk/pyGigEVision/blob/2de253135b8766c1eb752226539a16b810a1cf0f/pyGigEVision/gvsp.py#L55-L76), [L147](https://github.com/ladisk/pyGigEVision/blob/2de253135b8766c1eb752226539a16b810a1cf0f/pyGigEVision/gvsp.py#L147)).
- **Timestamps:** the raw 64-bit tick count from the leader packet ([gvsp.py#L614](https://github.com/ladisk/pyGigEVision/blob/2de253135b8766c1eb752226539a16b810a1cf0f/pyGigEVision/gvsp.py#L614)). It does not read the tick frequency or offer a latch.

### What it lacks
- **PTP:** no support at all. Searching for `ptp`/`1588` finds nothing.
- **Action commands:** none in the command table ([gvcp.py#L49-L56](https://github.com/ladisk/pyGigEVision/blob/2de253135b8766c1eb752226539a16b810a1cf0f/pyGigEVision/gvcp.py#L49-L56)).
- **Also missing:** WRITEMEM, events, multicast, chunk data, compressed/JPEG/H.264 payloads, and multi-part payloads.
- **Payload type:** read but never checked, so every block is treated as an uncompressed image.

### Hands-on: Docker with Aravis 0.8.26 `arv-fake-gv-camera-0.8`
1. **Discovery works.** But `bootstrap()` downloads 15,975 **zero bytes** instead of the XML. The camera's URL is `Local:arv-fake-camera.xml;10000;3e67`, and `parse_first_url` reads the digit-only hex `10000` as decimal ([genicam.py#L74-L79](https://github.com/ladisk/pyGigEVision/blob/2de253135b8766c1eb752226539a16b810a1cf0f/pyGigEVision/genicam.py#L74-L79)). A unit test asserts this decimal behaviour. Aravis always parses these fields as hex ([arvmisc.c#L1010-L1032](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/blob/0.8.26/src/arvmisc.c#L1010-L1032)).
2. **Frame grab works after a manual workaround**, writing hand-mapped registers.
   - With Linux default buffers: Mono8 640×480@30 gave 1 of 43 frames complete, and Mono16 gave 0 of 49.
   - Cause: the 16 MB `SO_RCVBUF` request is capped to 425,984 bytes, and the library silently ignores that ([gvsp.py#L347-L351](https://github.com/ladisk/pyGigEVision/blob/2de253135b8766c1eb752226539a16b810a1cf0f/pyGigEVision/gvsp.py#L347-L351)). Its docs do mention raising the OS buffer.
   - Aravis on the same fake camera got 91/91 and 82/82 complete.
   - With a 32 MB buffer forced through `SO_RCVBUFFORCE`, pyGigEVision got 100% complete frames.
3. **BayerRG8 and RGB8 frames come back wrong.** Both arrive as uint16 arrays of 614,400 bytes (expected 307,200 and 921,600) and are never marked complete.
4. **Throughput, one camera, 32 MB buffer:**
   - 1920×1080@100 with 1500-byte packets: 197 MB/s at about 49% of one core.
   - 2048×2048@60 with 9000-byte packets: 248 MB/s at about 21% of one core.
   - With the default capped buffer, pyGigEVision got 0% complete frames in all 4 configurations. Aravis's normal UDP socket path got 94% and 90% complete at 1500-byte packets, using 8–14% CPU.
5. **Two cameras in one process:** throughput falls to about 20 fps each at 1080p100, which points to GIL contention. **Two cameras in two processes:** each gets about 100% complete frames at about 200 MB/s.
6. **Too many resend requests.** I wrote a sender that drops nothing, paced at 110 MB/s (about 1 GigE). pyGigEVision still asked for **82.6% of all packets** to be resent. It counts every packet not yet received as missing once the frame is 5 ms old ([gvsp.py#L714-L730](https://github.com/ladisk/pyGigEVision/blob/2de253135b8766c1eb752226539a16b810a1cf0f/pyGigEVision/gvsp.py#L714-L730)). Aravis only flags packets below the highest one received ([arvgvstream.c#L644-L680](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/blob/0.8.26/src/arvgvstream.c#L644-L680)).
7. **Extended-ID streams (GigE Vision 2.x):** once the block ID passes 65535 and any packet is missing, `struct.pack('>HHII')` raises an uncaught error ([gvsp.py#L754](https://github.com/ladisk/pyGigEVision/blob/2de253135b8766c1eb752226539a16b810a1cf0f/pyGigEVision/gvsp.py#L754)). The receiver thread dies and `get_frame()` returns None forever, with no error reported.
8. **Frames of 5 MP or more** (2448×2048, 2592×1944) are silently dropped because of the 2048×2048 cap ([gvsp.py#L140-L145](https://github.com/ladisk/pyGigEVision/blob/2de253135b8766c1eb752226539a16b810a1cf0f/pyGigEVision/gvsp.py#L140-L145)).

The fake camera does not implement PACKETRESEND, PTP or action commands, so those paths could not be tested end to end.

### Why it is not a base for SkellyCam
- **Sync:** it has none of the sync pieces (PTP, action commands, timestamp handling).
- **No feature access by name:** you can't set things like `PtpEnable` or `PixelFormat` by name. That would need a full GenICam node-map engine written first.
- **Colour cameras:** they don't work.
- **Bugs:** several correctness bugs, including the silent receiver-thread crash.
- **Maintenance:** one main author and no commits for 3.5 months.

### What is worth reusing
- multi-NIC discovery
- the FORCEIP payload layout
- the GVCP ACK and retry handling
- the pre-allocated frame buffer pattern

These are compact and readable.

result.topic: rust-cpp-vendor: Non-Python (Rust/C/C++) and vendor-SDK options for GigE Vision capture, PTP and action commands
result.summary_markdown:
## Summary (survey date 2026-10-25)

The full notes, with every link, are in `C:/Users/Dom/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/c--Users-Dom-GitHub-freemocap-skellycam/f77e9c4e-e1ea-4406-8a36-bef826a63a0e/scratchpad/research/rust-cpp-vendor.md`. The test scripts are in `.../scratchpad/research/scripts/rust-cpp-vendor/`.

### Main findings
* **Best non-vendor options: two new pure-Rust GigE Vision stacks that ship Python wheels.** Both talk GVCP/GVSP directly over UDP and need no vendor SDK, so they work with any vendor's camera.
  * [viva-genicam](https://github.com/VitalyVorobyev/viva-genicam) (MIT, v0.10.0 on 2026-10-17). Wheels for win_amd64, macOS arm64 and manylinux x86_64.
  * [telegenic / `telegenicam`](https://github.com/valstad-shipworks/telegenic) (Apache-2.0, v2.1.0 on 2026-10-20). Wheels for win x64/arm64, macOS arm64 and Linux x64/aarch64.
  * I installed both from PyPI in Docker and streamed Mono8 frames from Aravis' `arv-fake-gv-camera-0.8`.
* **viva-genicam is the only open-source library I found that sends GVCP `ACTION_CMD`, including the scheduled variant.** See [action.rs#L17-L45](https://github.com/VitalyVorobyev/viva-genicam/blob/60c9c329a4175290b7065a74027c151cb0acd9ef/crates/viva-gige/src/action.rs#L17-L45) and the Python [`send_action`](https://github.com/VitalyVorobyev/viva-genicam/blob/60c9c329a4175290b7065a74027c151cb0acd9ef/crates/viva-pygenicam/src/gige.rs#L43-L67).
  * It also has a device-to-host timestamp fit, [`time_calibrate`](https://github.com/VitalyVorobyev/viva-genicam/blob/60c9c329a4175290b7065a74027c151cb0acd9ef/crates/viva-genicam/src/lib.rs#L394-L460).
  * Tested: its FakeGigeCamera did not acknowledge a command with the wrong keys (`acks=0`). With matching keys it acknowledged and acted (`acks=1, fake.actions()=1`).
  * Through generic `get()` I read the PTP node `GevIEEE1588OffsetFromMasterLatched_Val` on the fake.
* **cameleon has no GigE Vision support.** Its README says "supports only USB3 Vision" ([README#L28](https://github.com/cameleon-rs/cameleon/blob/1ab3fbf82a11f94da56e35a62893a6042054df4b/README.md#L28)), and its modules are only `camera/genapi/payload/u3v` ([lib.rs#L146-L150](https://github.com/cameleon-rs/cameleon/blob/1ab3fbf82a11f94da56e35a62893a6042054df4b/cameleon/src/lib.rs#L146-L150)).
  * Last release 0.1.14 on 2024-12-05.
  * The GigE work sits in open PRs [#198](https://github.com/cameleon-rs/cameleon/pull/198) and [#223](https://github.com/cameleon-rs/cameleon/pull/223).
* **Aravis (LGPL) cannot send action commands.** Its GVCP command enum has no ACTION_CMD ([arvgvcpprivate.h#L267-L281](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/blob/482547a3d56e3aa8d22d7ffed33c9f1588bfe17a/src/arvgvcpprivate.h#L267-L281)). The same limit applies to aravis-rs (0.11.1, 2025-02-10) and the GStreamer `aravissrc` element.
  * `aravissrc` works: tested with gst-launch, 5 buffers, bayer 512x512, EOS.
  * On main only (unreleased, commit 2026-10-03) it gained `add-reference-timestamp-meta`, which attaches the absolute device timestamp as `timestamp/x-ptp` ([gstaravis.c#L564-L567](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/blob/482547a3d56e3aa8d22d7ffed33c9f1588bfe17a/gst/gstaravis.c#L564-L567)).
* **rc_genicam_api (C++, BSD-3) runs on Linux and Windows only, with no macOS.**
  * It is a GenTL consumer that bundles the GenICam reference implementation and a closed-source Baumer GigE GenTL producer under the Baumer EULA. Its README says "GigE Vision 2.0 compatible" ([README#L4-L8](https://github.com/roboception/rc_genicam_api/blob/1f7aad7ab30d92ddd323992f9eb605b481aca252/README.md#L4-L8)).
  * PTP is toggled through `PtpEnable` / `PtpDataSetLatch` / `PtpStatus` / `PtpOffsetFromMaster` in [gc_config.cc#L280-L299](https://github.com/roboception/rc_genicam_api/blob/1f7aad7ab30d92ddd323992f9eb605b481aca252/tools/gc_config.cc#L280-L299).
* **Vendor SDKs mostly lock you to their own cameras:**
  * **Basler pylon:** the [EULA §4](https://docs.baslerweb.com/pylon-end-user-license-agreement) says "solely ... to operate a BASLER camera product".
  * **Spinnaker:** "supports FLIR and Dalsa ... cameras" ([product page](https://www.teledynevisionsolutions.com/products/spinnaker-sdk/)).
  * **LUCID Arena:** "supports all LUCID GigE Vision cameras" ([page](https://thinklucid.com/arena-software-development-kit/)).
  * **Allied Vision Vimba X** is the exception: "GenICam-compliant cameras and transport layers ... from all manufacturers", free of charge ([compatibility](https://docs.alliedvision.com/compatibility.html)). But the VmbPy wheels have no macOS build, and transport layers must be installed separately.
  * **Pleora eBUS** works with any vendor, but non-Pleora streams carry a watermark unless you buy a GEV-Rx license, plus a developer seat license ([eBUS Receive](https://www.pleora.com/?p=7076)).
* **PTP is configured with SFNC GenICam features on the camera in every library.** The names are `GevIEEE1588*` or `Ptp*`, for example in [Basler's PTP doc](https://docs.baslerweb.com/precision-time-protocol), [FLIR via the ROS driver](https://github.com/ros-drivers/flir_camera_driver/blob/a73f62c2b3bd23e2e555aa8ebf38f5f02187caf0/spinnaker_camera_driver/doc/index.rst#L320-L366) and [LUCID's app note](https://thinklucid.com/multi-camera-synchronization-using-ptp-and-scheduled-action-commands/). Any library with generic feature get/set can enable PTP. What differs between libraries:
  * whether they can send a (scheduled) action command;
  * whether they expose device timestamps per frame;
  * whether they provide a host-time mapping.

### Comparison table
| Option | Lang | License | Win/mac/Linux | Any vendor? | PTP features accessible | Action cmds | Last release |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| cameleon | Rust | MPL-2.0 | Y/Y/Y | **No GigE** (U3V only) | n/a | No | 0.1.14, 2024-12-05 |
| viva-genicam | Rust+Py | MIT | Y/Y(arm64)/Y(x64) | Yes | Yes (generic features + time_calibrate) | **Yes, incl. scheduled (tested)** | 0.10.0, 2026-10-17 |
| telegenic (telegenicam) | Rust+Py | Apache-2.0 | Y/Y(arm64)/Y | Yes | Yes (generic; frames carry device and host ns) | No | 2.1.0, 2026-10-20 |
| aravis-port | Rust | MIT/Apache | pure Rust (untested by me) | Yes | generic | No | 0.2.0, 2026-10-08 |
| aravis-rs → Aravis | Rust FFI | BSD-2 + LGPL | via Aravis | Yes | generic | No | 0.11.1, 2025-02-10 |

result.topic: frame-transport: how GigE Vision frames travel from camera to host (GVCP/GVSP), whether they arrive raw or compressed, bandwidth math, and a correction to the "GigE Vision 3 = PTP" premise
result.summary_markdown:
## Key findings

**1. The premise is wrong.** Single-cable PTP sync arrived with **GigE Vision 2.0, not 3.0**. A3's standard page says GEV 2.0 (Nov 2011) "enables transmission of compressed images (JPEG, JPEG 2000 and H.264), accurate synchronization of multi-camera systems". GEV 2.1 (Aug 2018) "includes an updated profile for IEEE1588". GEV 3.0 (TC-approved 17 Apr 2026) adds **GVRSP, RDMA streaming over RoCEv2**, as an optional alternative to GVSP ([A3 standard page](https://www.automate.org/vision/vision-standards/vision-standards-gige-vision), [A3 GEV 3.0 FAQ, 2026-08-19](https://www.automate.org/vision/blogs/gige-vision-3-0-standard-answers-to-frequently-asked-questions-faq)). The FAQ also says:
- "not all GigE Vision 3.0 cameras support RDMA"
- GEV 3.0 cameras support "GVSP v2" and GVRSP, but not legacy GVSP v1
- GVRSP needs a RoCEv2 NIC

The 1588 and scheduled-action bootstrap registers (0x096C to 0x097C) and ACTION_CMD 0x0100 are already in the 2.x register map ([Wireshark packet-gvcp.c#L120-L136](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/blob/98a6cfdba1ab23f3c835b17df802004bc9429040/epan/dissectors/packet-gvcp.c#L120-L136)). What you need is a GEV 2.x camera that implements IEEE 1588.

**2. How frames travel.**
- **GVCP** is the control channel: UDP requests to device port 3956 ([Aravis arvgvcpprivate.h#L36](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/blob/482547a3d56e3aa8d22d7ffed33c9f1588bfe17a/src/arvgvcpprivate.h#L36)). The host reads the GenICam XML and sets registers over it.
- **GVSP** is a one-way UDP stream to whatever host IP and port the host writes into the stream channel registers ([packet-gvcp.c#L148-L160](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/blob/98a6cfdba1ab23f3c835b17df802004bc9429040/epan/dissectors/packet-gvcp.c#L148-L160)):

| Register | Name | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| 0x0D00 | SCP | host port |
| 0x0D04 | SCPS | packet size, plus fire-test and do-not-fragment bits |
| 0x0D08 | SCPD | inter-packet delay, in timestamp ticks |
| 0x0D18 | SCDA | destination IP |

- **Packets per frame:** one leader, N payload packets, one trailer.
- **Header:** the standard 8-byte header has a 16-bit block id (frame id) and a 24-bit packet id. GEV 2.0 adds an extended-ID header (the EI bit, 0x80 in byte 4) with a 64-bit block id and 32-bit packet id ([Aravis arvgvspprivate.h#L132-L144](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/blob/482547a3d56e3aa8d22d7ffed33c9f1588bfe17a/src/arvgvspprivate.h#L132-L144), [packet-gvsp.c#L2349-L2450](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/blob/98a6cfdba1ab23f3c835b17df802004bc9429040/epan/dissectors/packet-gvsp.c#L2349-L2450)).
- **Payload type codes,** confirmed in both [Aravis arvbuffer.h#L79-L92](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/blob/482547a3d56e3aa8d22d7ffed33c9f1588bfe17a/src/arvbuffer.h#L79-L92) and [Wireshark packet-gvsp.c#L43-L54](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/blob/98a6cfdba1ab23f3c835b17df802004bc9429040/epan/dissectors/packet-gvsp.c#L43-L54):

| Code | Payload type |
|---|---|
| 0x0001 | IMAGE |
| 0x0002 | RAW |
| 0x0003 | FILE |
| 0x0004 | CHUNK |
| 0x0005 | EXT_CHUNK (deprecated) |
| 0x0006 | JPEG |
| 0x0007 | JPEG2000 |
| 0x0008 | H.264 |
| 0x0009 | MULTIZONE |
| 0x000A | MULTIPART |
| 0x000B | GenDC |
| 0x8000 and up | device-specific |

  Bit 0x4000 in the payload type means chunk data is appended.
- **Image leader** (36 bytes): flags, payload type, u64 timestamp, PFNC pixel format, size x/y, offset x/y, padding x/y. The trailer carries payload type and size y.

**Tested in Docker** with the Aravis 0.8.36 fake GigE Vision camera, tcpdump and tshark. The decoded leader was:
```
status 0, block 65401, LEADER, IMAGE, ts 0x18e1d68736273fd8, Mono8 0x01080001, 512x512
```
With SCPS 1400 a packet carries 1364 bytes of image data, so the trailer's packet_id is 194, exactly as predicted from the overhead formula in [arvgvspprivate.h#L257-L280](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/blob/482547a3d56e3aa8d22d7ffed33c9f1588bfe17a/src/arvgvspprivate.h#L257-L280).

**3. Packet loss.** The host sends PACKETRESEND_CMD 0x0040 over GVCP for packets it is missing ([arvgvcp.c#L405-L441](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/blob/482547a3d56e3aa8d22d7ffed33c9f1588bfe17a/src/arvgvcp.c#L405-L441)). Resent packets come back with status 0x0100. "Packet unavailable / removed from memory" errors (0x800C, 0x8011, 0x8012) stop further requests for that frame.
- **Resend depends on the camera.** Aravis turns resend off unless capability register 0x0934 bit 2 is set ([arvgvdevice.c#L2071-L2072](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/blob/482547a3d56e3aa8d22d7ffed33c9f1588bfe17a/src/arvgvdevice.c#L2071-L2072), [#L1904-L1905](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/blob/482547a3d56e3aa8d22d7ffed33c9f1588bfe17a/src/arvgvdevice.c#L1904-L1905)).
- **Docker, 2% simulated loss** (the fake camera has no resend): 0 resend requests and 19 of 20 frames failed.
- **Docker, 8000-byte packets:** with the default socket buffer 9 of 20 frames completed; with Aravis's auto `SO_RCVBUF` ([arvgvstream.c#L224-L262](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/blob/482547a3d56e3aa8d22d7ffed33c9f1588bfe17a/src/arvgvstream.c#L224-L262)) 21 of 21 completed. The host's socket buffer size matters.

**4. Raw or compressed?** Typical GigE Vision cameras send **uncompressed IMAGE payloads**: raw Bayer or Mono in PFNC formats.
- Aravis, the main open-source stack, gives JPEG, JPEG2000, H.264, multizone and GenDC payloads 0 expected packets and returns `PAYLOAD_NOT_SUPPORTED` ([arvgvstream.c#L278-L318, #L384-L393](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/blob/482547a3d56e3aa8d22d7ffed33c9f1588bfe17a/src/arvgvstream.c#L384-L393)).
- pyGigEVision only knows payload 0x0001 and Mono8 to Mono16 ([gvsp.py#L52-L76](https://github.com/ladisk/pyGigEVision/blob/2de253135b8766c1eb752226539a16b810a1cf0f/pyGigEVision/gvsp.py#L52-L76)). Any other pixel format falls back to 2 bytes per pixel ([#L226-L227](https://github.com/ladisk/pyGigEVision/blob/2de253135b8766c1eb752226539a16b810a1cf0f/pyGigEVision/gvsp.py#L226-L227)). From reading the code (not tested), it would mis-size BayerRG8 frames.

Compressed examples exist, but only one uses a standard GVSP payload type:

| Vendor / camera | Compression | How it is carried and decoded |
|---|---|---|
| [Baumer VLXT.I.JP](https://www.baumer.com/ca/en/service-support/technology-highlights/industrial-cameras-with-integrated-jpeg-image-compression/a/JPEG-image-compression) | JPEG | "based on the GigE Vision 2.0 standard per JPEG payload type"; Mono8 or YCbCr422_8 input; `ImageCompressionMode=JPEG` |
| [Teledyne FLIR Blackfly S GigE](https://www.teledynevisionsolutions.com/support/support-center/application-note/iis/using-lossless-compression/) | Lossless | "proprietary format", needs Spinnaker 2.4.0.143 or later |
| [Basler Compression Beyond](https://docs.baslerweb.com/compression-beyond) | Lossless or fixed-ratio lossy | Needs pylon `CImageDecompressor` plus a compression descriptor read from the camera |
| [LUCID QOI](https://support.thinklucid.com/knowledgebase/using_qoi_with_lucid_cameras/) | Lossless | Chosen as a `QOI_*` PixelFormat, decoded by Arena |

**5. Bandwidth** ([scripts-ft/bandwidth.py](file:///C:/Users/Dom/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/c--Users-Dom-GitHub-freemocap-skellycam/f77e9c4e-e1ea-4406-8a36-bef826a63a0e/scratchpad/research/scripts-ft/bandwidth.py)). Usable on 1 GbE: about 119.0 MB/s with 1500-byte packets, about 124.0 MB/s with jumbo frames.

| Stream | Payload | 1 GbE result |
|---|---|---|
| 1920x1200 BayerRG8 @ 60 fps | 138.24 MB/s = 1106 Mbit/s | **Not even one camera fits** (max about 51.6 fps, or 53.8 fps jumbo) |
| Same @ 30 fps | 553 Mbit/s | 1 camera per link (1.7) |
| Same @ 60 fps on other links | — | 2.5 GbE: 2.2 cameras; 5 GbE: 4.3; 10 GbE: 8.6 |

Multiple cameras sharing one link need SCPD or `DeviceLinkThroughputLimit` ([Beckhoff](https://infosys.beckhoff.com/content/1033/tf7xxx_tc3_vision/22185723659.html)).

**Stand-alone test for real cameras:** `scripts-ft/gvsp_pcap_report.py` (stdlib only, reads pcap and pcapng, runs on Windows, macOS and Linux). Capture with Wireshark while streaming, then run it. It reports payload type, pixel format, packet size and jumbo use, extended-ID mode, resends, timestamp deltas, and a compressed/not-compressed verdict. I validated it against the Docker captures.

result.topic: skellycam-arch: SkellyCam camera pipeline map and minimal GigE Vision backend integration design
result.summary_markdown:
I read SkellyCam at commit `23ccbf20` (branch `development`) and did not modify the repo. To verify behaviour I ran the existing test suite and two scripts in a fresh scratch venv. The repo's own `.venv` can't import the package because `polars` is missing (`skellycam/core/recorders/video_audio_remuxer.py:8`).

## 1. Worker processes and the capture loop
- **How a camera process is created:** HTTP `/camera/group/apply` → `CameraGroup.create` → `CameraManager.create` makes one `CameraStatus` and one `CameraWorker` per config, all sharing one `CameraOrchestrator` (`skellycam/core/camera/camera_manager.py:27-66`). `CameraWorker.create` **always** uses `opencv_camera_worker_method` as the target (`skellycam/core/camera/camera_worker.py:7,48-61`), so OpenCV is hard-wired here. The device is opened inside the child process (`setup_opencv_camera_loop.py:40`), which suits GigE SDK handles that can't be pickled.
- **Start-up:** each camera opens its device and publishes its *extracted* config. The parent sizes shared memory from those configs. All cameras then wait for each other (`all_ready`) while draining frames (`setup_opencv_camera_loop.py:42-65`; `camera_group.py:104-119`).
- **Each loop iteration:**
  - check for updates and pause;
  - **frame-count gate**: a camera may grab only if its frame count is ≤ every other camera's (`camera_orchestrator.py:96-109`; `opencv_camera_loop.py:67-69`);
  - `grab()` then `retrieve()` straight into the pre-allocated image, back to back in the same process (`opencv_get_frame.py:53-73`);
  - a text overlay is burned into the image, so it ends up in recorded video too (`:80-84`);
  - read recording flags before clearing `grabbing_frame` (`opencv_camera_loop.py:89-93`);
  - write the frame to the shared-memory ring buffer (overwrite allowed) (`:95-97`), record if needed (`:99-105`), then publish `frame_count` (`:116`).
- **No barrier between grab and retrieve.** The docstring says the split lets all cameras grab before any of them retrieves (`opencv_get_frame.py:30-33`), but the code has no cross-camera ordering between the two calls. The only cross-camera coordination is the frame-count gate, the start-up `all_ready` wait, and a wait for all cameras at recording start (`handle_recording_updates.py:45-47`).
- `frame_number` is a host-side count of successful grabs (`opencv_get_frame.py:79`), not a device frame ID.
- `check_framerate_reset` assumes 30 fps and re-creates the `cv2.VideoCapture` when frames run slow (`opencv_camera_loop.py:150-170`).

## 2. CameraConfig and backend choice
- **Fields:** `camera_id`, `camera_index` (used to open `cv2.VideoCapture` and must be unique), `camera_name`, `use_this_camera`, `resolution`, `color_channels=3`, `pixel_format="RGB"` (marked TODO and unused), `exposure_mode`, `exposure` (OpenCV log2 units), `framerate`, `rotation`, `capture_fourcc="MJPG"`, `writer_fourcc="X264"` (`camera_config.py:63-123,375-390`).
- **There is no backend abstraction.** `determine_backend.py` only picks which OpenCV video API to use: DSHOW, V4L2 or AVFoundation (`determine_backend.py:28-70`). The backend type aliases are OpenCV IDs (`type_overloads.py:12-13`). A grep for GigE, Aravis, Harvester, GenICam, PTP and vendor SDK names in `skellycam/`, `skellycam-ui/src` and `pyproject.toml` found nothing.

## 3. Frame record in shared memory
- A frame is `{frame_metadata, image: uint8[H,W,C]}` (`frame_dtype_factories.py:11-26`). Images are always uint8.
- Metadata holds `camera_info`, `frame_number`, `timebase_mapping`, and nine lifecycle timestamps, all host `time.perf_counter_ns()` (`numpy_record_dtypes.py:10-33,222-228`).
- UTC conversion uses a single `(time_ns, perf_counter_ns)` sample taken when the camera group's IPC object is created (`timebase_mapping.py:16-32`; `camera_group_ipc.py:24`). The docs say it is created at recording start; that is wrong.
- **There is no field for a device or PTP timestamp, or a device frame ID.**
- Downstream code assumes 3-channel BGR uint8:
  - JPEG encode for the UI (`frontend_payload_bytearray.py:142`);
  - `cv2.VideoWriter` with colour on by default, and PyAV with `bgr24` (`video_recorder.py:124-130`; `pyav_video_writer.py:27`);
  - recording validation compares the decoded video shape to `config.image_shape`. For mono that is `(H,W)` while the buffer holds `(H,W,1)` (verified), so mono doesn't work end to end.
- Each camera gets a 1 GiB ring buffer (`ring_buffer_shared_memory.py:35-45`). Measured depth: 388 frames at 1280×720, 71 at 2448×2048.

## 4. Device detection
- `detect_available_cameras` uses `cv2_enumerate_cameras` (`detect_cameras_devices.py:86-109`) and returns `CameraDeviceInfo` rows (index, name, VID, PID, path, backend). `camera_id` is a hash of path or VID/PID (`:35-55`).
- These are served at `POST /camera/detect` (`camera_router.py:89-100`).
- The UI builds each camera's config from `(camera_id, index, name)` only (`skellycam-ui/src/store/slices/cameras/cameras-thunks.ts:63-97`).
- GigE devices would be added as extra `CameraDeviceInfo` rows carrying backend, serial, MAC and IP. The UI must then carry backend and serial through to the config.

## 5. Recording and timestamp CSVs
- During recording, each recorder keeps a copy of every frame's metadata (`video_recorder.py:108`) and sends the list to the parent when recording stops. The parent then runs the finalizer.
- Per-camera CSVs auto-map **every** lifecycle-timestamp field to a column, subtracting the host-clock recording start (`create_camera_csvs.py:85-89`).
- The multi-camera CSV computes `inter_camera.frame_grab_range.ms` from host grab midpoints (`create_multi_frame_csvs.py:54-58`).
- **Where PTP timestamps should go:** a new `device_timing` sub-record in the frame metadata, not the lifecycle-timestamp dtype (otherwise a device-clock value gets a host-clock offset subtracted). It needs explicit `device.*` CSV columns plus `inter_camera.device_timestamp_range.ms`.
- Dead, buggy code: `create_camera_frame_csv_row_recarray` (`create_camera_csvs.py:110-178`) has no callers and adds `pre_grab` to itself instead of `post_grab`.

## 6. Tests and mocks
Full suite: 171 passed, 15 failed, 4 errors in 8.7s. The interpreter then hangs on exit.
- **Most failures are beartype type checks.** `beartype_this_package()` (`skellycam/__init__.py:16-17`) rejects `MagicMock` objects and int-vs-float mismatches.
- `MockVideoCapture` has no `grab`/`retrieve`, so it can't drive the capture loop (`tests/mocks/camera_mock.py:8-118`).
- Patterns worth reusing:
  - real frame recarrays built from configs (`test_frontend_payload_and_recording.py:28-49`);
  - orchestrator tested without processes (`test_camera_orchestrator.py:10-12`);
  - a small shared-memory ring buffer (`test_shared_memory.py:140-151`);
  - thread-mode workers (`test_worker_lifecycle.py`);
  - patching the detect function in router tests (`test_camera_router.py:10-31`).

## 7. Proposed design
- **Backend interface:** add `skellycam/core/camera/backends/` with a `@runtime_checkable` `CameraBackend` Protocol: `open`, `apply_config`, `start`, `drain`, `grab`, `retrieve(out)`, `device_timing`, `is_open`, `close`.
  - Generalize the loop and worker entry point to call it, keeping the gate, flag ordering and shared-memory code unchanged.
  - Wrap the existing OpenCV helpers as `OpenCVBackend`, and put the GigE implementation under an optional install extra.
- **Prototype check:**
  - Beartype accepts a fake backend checked against a `@runtime_checkable` Protocol and rejects a non-conforming object.
  - A plain Protocol (without `@runtime_checkable`) used as a type hint fails as soon as the function is decorated.
- **CameraConfig:** add `backend="opencv"` (default), `device_id` (serial), `device_address`, `source_pixel_format`, `ptp_enabled`. Give GigE cameras synthetic, non-colliding `camera_index` values.
- **Debayer:** `cv2.cvtColor(raw, code, dst=frame.image[0])` writes in place into the shared-memory slot (verified). It took about 0.18 ms at 2448×2048 on this machine.
  - **OpenCV's Bayer names don't match the layout names.** For an RGGB mosaic, `COLOR_BayerBG2BGR` gives red; `COLOR_BayerRG2BGR` gives blue.
  - Use `Mono8` → `GRAY2BGR`, and prefer 8-bit pixel formats.
- **PTP timestamps:** fill `device_timing` after `grab()`. It then flows through shared memory, the recorder, the recording-finished message and the finalizer into new CSV columns. Compare device frame IDs against `frame_number` to detect dropped frames.

result.topic: ptp-sync: IEEE 1588 PTP multi-camera synchronization on GigE Vision, end to end
result.summary_markdown:
## Summary

**The premise needs correcting: PTP did not arrive with GigE Vision 3.** IEEE 1588 PTP and scheduled action commands both date from **GigE Vision 2.0**. Wireshark's GVCP dissector tags every IEEE 1588 bootstrap field and the scheduled-action flag and time as `_v2_0`, and `GEV_STATUS_ACTION_LATE` carries the comment `/* GEV 2.0 */` ([packet-gvcp.c](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/blob/02dbbdbf41aecc1f2a4ba6c0db2546af5bb07d75/epan/dissectors/packet-gvcp.c#L204-229)). Aravis issue [#184](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/issues/184), opened in 2018, says the same: "GigEVision 2.0 introduces Action Commands…". So single-cable PTP sync works with ordinary GEV 2.x cameras, including PoE ones.

### 1. Turning PTP on in the camera
- **Standard features:** GenICam SFNC 2.8 (2026-04-08), §27.3, defines `PtpEnable`, `PtpDataSetLatch`, `PtpStatus`, `PtpServoStatus`, `PtpOffsetFromMaster` (ns), `PtpClockAccuracy` and the clock-ID features.
  - `PtpStatus` values are Initializing, Faulty, Disabled, Listening, PreMaster, Master, Passive, Uncalibrated, Slave (numbered 1-9).
  - The values are *latched*: execute `PtpDataSetLatch` first, then read them.
  - The older names `GevIEEE1588`, `GevIEEE1588Status`, `GevTimestampControlLatch` and `GevTimestampValue` are deprecated in favour of `PtpEnable`, `PtpStatus`, `TimestampLatch` and `TimestampLatchValue`.
- **Register level** ([Wireshark](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/blob/02dbbdbf41aecc1f2a4ba6c0db2546af5bb07d75/epan/dissectors/packet-gvcp.c#L3468-3500)):
  - capability register `0x0934`, bit `0x00080000`
  - enable bit in configuration register `0x0954`, bit `0x00080000`
  - status register `0x096C`
- **Vendor quirks:**
  - **Basler:** PTP is always off at power-up, and enabling it changes the tick from 125 MHz to 1 ns. Check the *maximum* offset over a time window, because it does not fall steadily.
  - **Allied Vision:** uses `PtpMode` Off/Slave/Master/Auto, and documents PtpStatus as 0-based. Read the enumeration by name, not by integer value.
  - **LUCID:** uses `PtpSlaveOnly` and supports end-to-end delay measurement only.

### 2. Who becomes grandmaster
- **No host master is needed.** The cameras run the Best Master Clock Algorithm among themselves (Basler: lowest Priority1 wins; Allied Vision: Auto; LUCID: BMC).
- **Linux host as master:** possible with `ptp4l` (linuxptp v4.4; defaults are UDPv4, E2E delay, hardware timestamping; `-S` for software timestamping, `serverOnly`, `priority1`; [man page](https://github.com/richardcochran/linuxptp/blob/f98cb5de87e63696599c59d0a9df7dc04d08d40d/ptp4l.8#L48-L62)). Allied Vision warns that host software masters gave "significant jitter".
- **Windows:** the built-in PTP is a *client* ("subordinate") only, available from Windows 10 1809 and Server 2019 ([W32Time README](https://github.com/microsoft/W32Time/blob/9795ef91dfe5a452266ffd8106ff2bcb17f33556/README.md#L25-L36)).
- **macOS:** I could not find a supported option.

### 3. Network requirements
- PTP runs over UDP 319/320, multicast to 224.0.1.129.
- **IGMP snooping blocks Basler camera PTP**, because the cameras don't join any group. Basler says the only fix is to disable snooping ([KB](https://docs.baslerweb.com/knowledge/ptp-synchronization-doesn't-work-when-igmp-snooping-is-enabled)).
- Allied Vision says all cameras should be on the same subnet behind one switch. Basler recommends PTP-capable switches.
- **Accuracy figures from vendors:**
  - Allied Vision: "within two microseconds"; under ±1 µs over 69 hours; about 125 ns on an oscilloscope.
  - Teledyne: "a few microseconds".
  - LUCID: the sample output in its app note implies about 9.2 µs across 7 cameras. That is my arithmetic; LUCID states no figure.

### 4. How exposures get aligned
Synced clocks alone don't align exposures. There are three methods:
- **(a) Scheduled Action Commands.**
  - Camera setup: `TriggerSource=Action1` plus `ActionDeviceKey`, `ActionGroupKey` and `ActionGroupMask` (SFNC §14).
  - The host sends GVCP `ACTION_CMD 0x0100` to UDP 3956. Header: `0x42`, flags (`0x80` = scheduled, `0x01` = ack required), command, length (12 or 20), request id. Payload: device_key, group_key, group_mask, then an optional u64 action_time ([dissector](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/blob/02dbbdbf41aecc1f2a4ba6c0db2546af5bb07d75/epan/dissectors/packet-gvcp.c#L2092-2114)).
  - The action time is a latched timestamp plus a delay (Basler procedure).
- **(b) Vendor firmware modes:**
  - Basler Synchronous Free Run (`SyncFreeRunTimerStartTimeLow/High`, `SyncFreeRunTimerTriggerRateAbs`)
  - LUCID `AcquisitionStartMode=PTPSync` + `PTPSyncFrameRate`, which "schedules 4 advance action commands in the firmware"
  - Allied Vision `PtpAcquisitionGateTime` + FixedRate
- **(c) Post-hoc matching:** use the 64-bit timestamp in every GVSP leader ([Aravis](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/blob/482547a3d56e3aa8d22d7ffed33c9f1588bfe17a/src/arvgvspprivate.h#L452-L463)) or `ChunkTimestamp`.
  - Caveat: Aravis reads the tick frequency only once, when the stream is created ([L1617](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/blob/482547a3d56e3aa8d22d7ffed33c9f1588bfe17a/src/arvgvstream.c#L1617)). Enable PTP before creating streams.

### 5. Mapping camera time to host time
- Execute `TimestampLatch` (bootstrap: write 2 to `0x0944`, read `0x0948`/`0x094C`) with host clock reads just before and after. The error is roughly half the round-trip time.
- Alternatively, on Linux, make the host the PTP grandmaster.

### Which software can send action commands
- **Aravis:** no API. There is no ACTION_CMD in the [command enum](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/blob/482547a3d56e3aa8d22d7ffed33c9f1588bfe17a/src/arvgvcpprivate.h#L267-L281), and the fake camera doesn't handle it ([source](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/blob/482547a3d56e3aa8d22d7ffed33c9f1588bfe17a/src/arvgvfakecamera.c#L157-L216)). Issue #184 is still open.
- **pypylon:** has `ActionCommand` and `ScheduledActionCommand` ([GigETransportLayer.i](https://github.com/basler/pypylon/blob/079cd1c7b7a9222591c69f88e3001059eca50dfe/src/pylon/GigETransportLayer.i#L230-L365)).
- **GenTL producers:** the GenTL SFNC 1.2 interface features `ActionCommand`, `ActionScheduledTime` and `GevActionDestinationIPAddress` are reachable through harvesters' `ia.interface.node_map`. Whether each producer implements them is unverified.
- **pyGigEVision v0.2.2:** no action or PTP support, but it can write the registers above.
- **Raw UDP in about 10 lines of Python:** my packets decode correctly in tshark.

### Tests
**Run here in Docker** (ubuntu 24.04, tshark 4.2.2, aravis-tools 0.8.30):
1. Generated ACTION_CMD packets decode correctly in tshark (flags `0x81`, device key, group key, mask, scheduled time).
2. The Aravis fake GigE Vision camera reports capability `0x0` and returns 0 from the timestamp latch. It doesn't answer ACTION_CMD, and `arv-tool` finds no Ptp, Action or Timestamp features. **PTP cannot be emulated, so real cameras are required.**
3. The fake camera's GVSP leader timestamps fall inside the host's time window and equal `g_get_real_time()*1000`. This confirms how the leader timestamp field works.

result.topic: harvesters-gentl: GenICam GenTL route (Harvesters + genicam + GigE Vision GenTL producers)
result.summary_markdown:
## Bottom line
Harvesters plus the EMVA `genicam` bindings is a workable, vendor-neutral Python consumer. It is a thin layer, though: the transport, the Windows performance filter driver, PTP support and action-command sending all live in the **GenTL producer (.cti)**, and there is no free, vendor-neutral GigE Vision producer with full features on every OS.

I ran the stack end to end in Docker with two test setups: an Aravis fake camera behind the MIT-licensed `viva_gentl.cti`, and the `viky.cti` simulator that ships inside the genicam wheel. It works. The runs also found two practical problems:
- **GIL:** [Harvesters#508](https://github.com/genicam/harvesters/issues/508) is confirmed (`fetch()` holds the GIL), so SkellyCam would need one process per camera.
- **`timestamp_frequency` bug:** `Buffer.timestamp_frequency` raises an uncaught `AttributeError` when the producer gives no ns timestamps.

## Harvesters status
- **Last release:** 1.4.3 on 2024-05-16. `master` has not moved since 2024-05-08 ([tag commit](https://github.com/genicam/harvesters/tree/383494e36ebb80e2daa271ac0e980dde2093970c)).
- **Unreleased work:** branch `dev-gendc` (last commit 2026-04-01) is versioned 1.5.0. It requires Python >=3.10, `genicam>=1.6.0` and numpy>=2 ([pyproject](https://github.com/genicam/harvesters/blob/86a93095ebb38309ff6320ccefe3a8e2a23cada9/pyproject.toml)).
- **Licence:** Apache-2.0. Supported Python versions are "defined by the genicam package" ([INSTALL.rst L23](https://github.com/genicam/harvesters/blob/383494e36ebb80e2daa271ac0e980dde2093970c/docs/INSTALL.rst#L23)).

## `genicam` wheels (from the PyPI JSON)
- **1.6.0 (2026-09-01):** cp310–cp314 for win_amd64, manylinux2014 x86_64/aarch64/armv7l and **macosx_13_0_arm64**.
- **1.5.1:** has no macOS wheels.
- **Intel Mac:** the last macOS x86_64 wheel was 1.3.0 (2023).
- **Licence:** the EMVA GenICam License. It is a modified BSD that allows free binary redistribution but no modification.
- **Linux catch:** the wheel links to `libpython3.12.so.1.0`, so a stock ubuntu:24.04 venv needs `libpython3.12t64` installed (I hit this in testing).

## How frames arrive
Code references are from [core.py @1.4.3](https://github.com/genicam/harvesters/blob/383494e36ebb80e2daa271ac0e980dde2093970c/src/harvesters/core.py).
- **Fetching:** `fetch()` ([L2520-L2568](https://github.com/genicam/harvesters/blob/383494e36ebb80e2daa271ac0e980dde2093970c/src/harvesters/core.py#L2520-L2568)) is a Python loop that polls `update_event_data` with a 1 ms timeout ([L1703](https://github.com/genicam/harvesters/blob/383494e36ebb80e2daa271ac0e980dde2093970c/src/harvesters/core.py#L1703), [L2412-L2473](https://github.com/genicam/harvesters/blob/383494e36ebb80e2daa271ac0e980dde2093970c/src/harvesters/core.py#L2412-L2473)).
- **Image data:** `Component2DImage` wraps the producer's buffer with **zero-copy `numpy.frombuffer`** and unpacks the PFNC pixel format ([L904-L977](https://github.com/genicam/harvesters/blob/383494e36ebb80e2daa271ac0e980dde2093970c/src/harvesters/core.py#L904-L977)). Leaving the `with` block hands the buffer back to the producer, so copy anything you keep.
- **Raw or compressed:** Harvesters recognises JPEG, JPEG2000 and H264 payload types but has no decoder for them ([L1272-L1325](https://github.com/genicam/harvesters/blob/383494e36ebb80e2daa271ac0e980dde2093970c/src/harvesters/core.py#L1272-L1325)). The GigE test stream arrived as uncompressed `PAYLOAD_TYPE_IMAGE` Mono8.
- **Timestamps:** `timestamp_ns` comes from GenTL `BUFFER_INFO_TIMESTAMP_NS`, which [GenTL 1.6](https://www.emva.org/wp-content/uploads/GenICam_GenTL_1_6.pdf) (p. 147) requires producers to convert to ns ([L1193-L1235](https://github.com/genicam/harvesters/blob/383494e36ebb80e2daa271ac0e980dde2093970c/src/harvesters/core.py#L1193-L1235)).
- **Chunk data:** it is attached automatically to `remote_device.node_map` on each fetch ([L2327-L2377](https://github.com/genicam/harvesters/blob/383494e36ebb80e2daa271ac0e980dde2093970c/src/harvesters/core.py#L2327-L2377)). I confirmed this with viky.
- **Padding bug:** at [L974](https://github.com/genicam/harvesters/blob/383494e36ebb80e2daa271ac0e980dde2093970c/src/harvesters/core.py#L974) the result of `numpy.delete` is thrown away, so line padding is not stripped.
- **Multi-camera:** create one ImageAcquirer per device ([upstream test](https://github.com/genicam/harvesters/blob/383494e36ebb80e2daa271ac0e980dde2093970c/src/harvesters/test/test_harvester_core.py#L162-L200)). A camera visible through several network cards is listed once per card, so de-duplicate by serial number. Otherwise opening the duplicate fails because the first handle has exclusive control (observed in testing).

## GIL test (run4)
I fetched at 25 fps in a background thread and measured an unrelated Python thread:
- **Default 1 ms poll:** its throughput halved and its wake-up latency went from 0.05 ms to 5–20 ms.
- **50 ms poll:** throughput fell to about 1/8 and wake-up latency was about 40 ms, one frame period. That shows the GIL is held while the C call is blocked.

## PTP and action commands through Harvesters
- **PTP is a camera feature.** It is SFNC 2.8 §27.3 (`PtpEnable`, `PtpStatus`, `PtpOffsetFromMaster`; all Optional). `GevIEEE1588` is deprecated ([SFNC 2.8](https://www.emva.org/wp-content/uploads/GenICam_SFNC_v2_8.pdf) pp. 529–552). You reach it through `ia.remote_device.node_map`.
- **Camera-side action setup:** SFNC ch. 14 (`TriggerSource=Action1`, Action keys and mask).
- **Host-side sending** belongs to the GenTL **Interface module**. [GenTL SFNC 1.2](https://www.emva.org/wp-content/uploads/GenICam_GenTL_SFNC_1_2.pdf) §2.2.3/§3.2.3 (pp. 26, 72–75) defines `ActionCommand`, `ActionDeviceKey/GroupKey/GroupMask`, `ActionScheduledTimeEnable/Time` and `GevActionDestinationIPAddress`, all **Recommended**, not Mandatory. Harvesters exposes `ia.interface.node_map`, so action commands work only if the producer implements these features.
- **Producer support:**
  - Balluff mvGenTLProducer: yes.
  - Allied Vision VimbaGigETL: yes, including scheduled actions.
  - The Imaging Source: has `ActionCommandToAllInterfaces`.
  - Basler pylon: "The GenTL producer for GigE Vision does not support action commands" ([26.06 notes](https://docs.baslerweb.com/pylon-software-suite-26-06-release-notes)).
  - viva-gentl: none of the action features (tested).

## Producer catalogue (details in notes)
- **Balluff/MATRIX VISION Impact Acquire 3.7.2 (2026-07-27):**
  - Covers Windows, Linux x64/arm64/armhf and **macOS ARM64**, and includes a Windows NDIS filter driver.
  - 3.7.0 added "full GEV 3.0 support including RoCEv2 (RDMA)".
  - Since 3.0.0, third-party devices need a licence: "an overlay will be added to each image once 200 have been captured" ([versionInfo](https://static.matrix-vision.com/mvIMPACT_Acquire/3.7.2/versionInfo.txt)).
- **Basler:** the EULA says it may be used "solely ... to operate a BASLER camera product", so it is vendor-locked.
- **Baumer GAPI:** vendor-neutral for GigE ([wiki](https://github.com/genicam/harvesters/wiki), [rc_genicam_api#8](https://github.com/roboception/rc_genicam_api/issues/8)). The 2019 EULA is permissive.
- **Allied Vision Vimba X:** free, with a filter driver and macOS support. Whether its GigE layer accepts other vendors' cameras is unclear.
- **Spinnaker:** supports Teledyne/FLIR/Dalsa cameras, including on Apple Silicon.
- **Pleora eBUS:** unlicensed receive adds a watermark, and its datasheet does not mention a GenTL producer.
- **Euresys Gigelink:** "any GigE Vision camera", paid add-on.
- **The Imaging Source:** a free producer, described as being for TIS cameras.
- **viva_gentl.cti:** MIT licensed, for Linux, macOS arm64 and Windows, with no filter driver. Merged 2026-10-12 and tested here.

## Stand-alone tests delivered
`scripts/harvesters-gentl/`:
- `probe_harvesters.py`: lists cameras and features and fetches frames.
- `ptp_action_harvesters.py`: enables PTP, sends scheduled action commands from each interface, and reports the timestamp spread across cameras.
- `gil_probe.py`: reproduces the GIL test.

The folder also has the Dockerfile and the run logs.

I did not run any vendor producer. Their installers or EULAs require accepting a licence, and I did not do that on the user's behalf.

missed_important_points: The stream-channel packet-size constants in pyGigEVision are wrong, and a unit test locks them in. standard.py L33-35 defines SC_PACKET_SIZE_MASK=0xFFFC, SC_SCPS_DO_NOT_FRAGMENT=1<<1 and SC_SCPS_FIRE_TEST_PACKET=1<<0 (https://github.com/ladisk/pyGigEVision/blob/2de253135b8766c1eb752226539a16b810a1cf0f/pyGigEVision/standard.py#L27-L37). The GigE Vision register uses MSB-first bit numbering. Wireshark's dissector has FireTestPacket=0x80000000, DoNotFragment=0x40000000, PixelEndianness=0x20000000 and PacketSize=0x0000FFFF (https://github.com/wireshark/wireshark/blob/40d923914bcbd1818ea5ebb3cb6b5b3b020fe875/epan/dissectors/packet-gvcp.c#L3825-L3847). Aravis agrees (https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/blob/0.8.26/src/arvgvcpprivate.h#L126-L135). Writing SC_SCPS_FIRE_TEST_PACKET would therefore change the packet size instead of firing a test packet.

Extended-ID (GEV 2.x) PACKETRESEND is malformed even for block ids at or below 65535. pyGigEVision always sends the legacy 12-byte payload with flag byte 0x01. Bytes captured in Docker: 42010040000c0001000000070000000500000005 (https://github.com/ladisk/pyGigEVision/blob/2de253135b8766c1eb752226539a16b810a1cf0f/pyGigEVision/gvsp.py#L739-L767). Aravis sets the EXTENDED_IDS flag and uses a 20-byte payload with a 64-bit block id (https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/blob/0.8.26/src/arvgvcp.c#L404-L439). Wireshark's dissector does the same (https://github.com/wireshark/wireshark/blob/40d923914bcbd1818ea5ebb3cb6b5b3b020fe875/epan/dissectors/packet-gvcp.c#L1555-L1619). Aravis also sends resend requests with packet_flags 0 (no ACK requested). pyGigEVision's GVCPClient.send_packetresend instead goes through _send_cmd with FLAG_ACK and waits for an ACK (https://github.com/ladisk/pyGigEVision/blob/2de253135b8766c1eb752226539a16b810a1cf0f/pyGigEVision/gvcp.py#L892-L925).

RGB8 corruption is silent. Frames come back flagged complete=True but truncated to 614,400 bytes of uint16 instead of 921,600 bytes of RGB (89/89 frames in my run). A caller that filters on info['complete'] will not catch it (https://github.com/ladisk/pyGigEVision/blob/2de253135b8766c1eb752226539a16b810a1cf0f/pyGigEVision/gvsp.py#L164-L197).

Packet reordering causes loss. Data packets that arrive before the leader are never written, because _raw_buffer is None until the leader arrives (gvsp.py L160). The leader handler then replaces the per-block buffer with a fresh one (https://github.com/ladisk/pyGigEVision/blob/2de253135b8766c1eb752226539a16b810a1cf0f/pyGigEVision/gvsp.py#L608-L632).

The FIRST_URL hex question is settled by the GenTL 1.6 standard (section 4.1.2.1, Table 4-1). The address and length in a 'local:' URL 'must be expressed in hexadecimal form without a prefix', and the form without '///' is described as 'compatible to the GigE Vision local format' (https://www.emva.org/wp-content/uploads/GenICam_GenTL_1_6.pdf, 2,893,325 bytes, fetched 2026-10-25). pyGigEVision's decimal-first parsing therefore goes against the spec.

result.topic: from-scratch: assessing a home-grown GigE Vision client for SkellyCam (pure Python vs Rust+PyO3 vs C++ with bindings)
result.summary_markdown:
## Bottom line
A from-scratch **transport** (GVCP control plus GVSP streaming) is small and well documented. I built a pure-Python, stdlib-only client in about 830 lines (`tests/gev_scratch_probe.py`). In Docker it discovered Aravis's software GigE camera (`arv-fake-gv-camera-0.8`), took control, fetched the GenICam XML and streamed **75/75 complete frames**.

There are two hard parts:
1. **GenApi evaluation.** This means turning the camera's XML description into readable and writable features.
2. **Keeping packet loss at zero.** This depends on socket receive-buffer limits and, in Python, the GIL.

PTP needs no new protocol code. It is a few bootstrap registers, or the equivalent GenApi features.

**Premise correction.** IEEE 1588 (PTP) arrived in **GigE Vision 2.0**, not 3.0. Wireshark names the capability bit `hf_gvcp_capability_1588_v2_0` (mask 0x00080000) and the enable bit `..._1588_enable_v2_0` in register 0x0954 ([packet-gvcp.c L3474-3477, L3604-3607](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/blob/98a6cfdba1ab23f3c835b17df802004bc9429040/epan/dissectors/packet-gvcp.c#L3474-3477)). GigE Vision 3.0 (released 2026-05-12) adds RoCEv2/RDMA streaming (GVRSP), per the [press release](https://www.vision-systems.com/directory/software/machine-vision-imaging-software/press-release/55377111/association-for-advancing-automation-a3-a3-officially-releases-gige-vision-30-opening-new-possibilities-in-machine-vision). Pure Python can't implement GVRSP, and none of the open-source stacks I checked support it.

## Minimum protocol surface (permalinks in notes)
- **Commands.** Codes 0x0002 through 0x0101 are listed in [Wireshark L177-197](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/blob/98a6cfdba1ab23f3c835b17df802004bc9429040/epan/dissectors/packet-gvcp.c#L177-197). Aravis's enum has neither FORCEIP nor ACTION.
- **Discovery.** The acknowledgement field offsets are in [Wireshark L2121-2195](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/blob/98a6cfdba1ab23f3c835b17df802004bc9429040/epan/dissectors/packet-gvcp.c#L2121-2195).
- **Bootstrap registers** are in Aravis [arvgvcpprivate.h L38-137](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/blob/482547a3d56e3aa8d22d7ffed33c9f1588bfe17a/src/arvgvcpprivate.h#L38-L137):
  - control-channel privilege (CCP) at 0x0A00
  - heartbeat timeout at 0x0938
  - XML URL at 0x0200
  - stream channel 0 at 0x0D00, 0x0D04 and 0x0D18
- **XML fetch.** The `Local:` URL and zip handling are in [arvgvdevice.c L1266-1397](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/blob/482547a3d56e3aa8d22d7ffed33c9f1588bfe17a/src/arvgvdevice.c#L1266-L1397).
- **Packet-size negotiation** (fire-test packet with do-not-fragment, binary search): [L614-784](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/blob/482547a3d56e3aa8d22d7ffed33c9f1588bfe17a/src/arvgvdevice.c#L614-L784).
- **Packet resend**, including the 64-bit block-ID form: [arvgvcp.c L406-440](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/blob/482547a3d56e3aa8d22d7ffed33c9f1588bfe17a/src/arvgvcp.c#L406-L440).
- **Stream headers** (GVSP, standard and extended IDs): [arvgvspprivate.h](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/blob/482547a3d56e3aa8d22d7ffed33c9f1588bfe17a/src/arvgvspprivate.h#L132-L192).
- **Missing-packet logic:** [arvgvstream.c L659-746](https://github.com/AravisProject/aravis/blob/482547a3d56e3aa8d22d7ffed33c9f1588bfe17a/src/arvgvstream.c#L659-L746).
- **ACTION_CMD**: device key, group key, group mask, plus a 64-bit time when flag 0x80 is set ([Wireshark L2092-2115](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/blob/98a6cfdba1ab23f3c835b17df802004bc9429040/epan/dissectors/packet-gvcp.c#L2092-2115)). Only viva-genicam implements it ([action.rs](https://github.com/VitalyVorobyev/viva-genicam/blob/60c9c329a4175290b7065a74027c151cb0acd9ef/crates/viva-gige/src/action.rs#L17-L211)).

**Raw or compressed.** Frames arrive raw by default: payload type 1 is image data in a standard (PFNC) pixel format. GEV 2.0 also defines JPEG, JPEG2000 and H.264 payload types ([packet-gvsp.c L43-54](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/blob/98a6cfdba1ab23f3c835b17df802004bc9429040/epan/dissectors/packet-gvsp.c#L43-54)). Every image leader packet carries a 64-bit device timestamp.

**PTP.** Controlled and read through registers:
- capability 0x0934, bit 0x00080000
- enable 0x0954, bit 0x00080000
- status 0x096C, low 4 bits
- profiles 0x0974–0x097C

A real Hikrobot XML maps `GevIEEE1588` to bit 12 of the register at 0x0954 and `GevIEEE1588Status` to 0x096C bits 31..28 ([Hikrobot.xml L51846-51900](https://github.com/valstad-shipworks/telegenic/blob/eb9de6579dde096b4a60ccead934edcc3795d6c3/tests/data/Hikrobot.xml#L51846-L51900)). Both match the Wireshark masks under GenApi's big-endian bit numbering.

## GenApi is the hard part
I counted node types in real camera XMLs (from telegenic's test data):

| XML | Nodes | SwissKnife formulas | Converters | Selectors | Availability predicates | Invalidators | Computed addresses |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hikrobot | 2165 | 283 | 58 | 41 | 406 | 370 | 513 |
| Imperx | 1386 | 402 | — | 7 | 193 | 392 | 11 |

- My toy formula translator parses 93–97% of the formulas. The failures are nested `?:`.
- Parsing is the easy part; selectors, invalidation and computed addresses are not.
- Existing evaluators are large: about 14.7k lines of C in Aravis, 11.8k lines of Rust in cameleon-genapi, 21.5k in viva-genicam's two GenApi crates.
- pyGigEVision (v0.2.2, MIT, 2026-07-08) has **no** evaluator. Its README tells users to write vendor registers themselves ([README L30-47](https://github.com/ladisk/pyGigEVision/blob/2de253135b8766c1eb752226539a16b810a1cf0f/README.rst#L30-L47)).
- **Tested working:** the official EMVA `genicam` 1.6.0 wheel's NodeMap, driven through an `AbstractPort` subclass on top of my pure-Python control client (the harvesters pattern, [port.py L31-67](https://github.com/genicam/harvesters/blob/383494e36ebb80e2daa271ac0e980dde2093970c/src/harvesters/_private/core/port.py#L31-L67)). It evaluated PayloadSize and executed AcquisitionStart.
- **Wheel caveats:**
  - On Linux it needs the shared `libpython3.12.so`.
  - There is no macOS x86_64 wheel.
  - It is under the GenICam license.

## Performance (measured; scripts saved)
**Line rate at 1 GbE:** 81,274 packets/s at MTU 1500 and 13,830 at MTU 9000. At 10 GbE: 813k and 138k.

**`udp_recv_benchmark.py`, loopback:**
- At 1 Gbit/s, one Python receiver with a 16 MiB buffer has **0% drops** at about 21–34% of one core (MTU 1500) and 5–8% (MTU 9000).
- The single-thread ceiling is about 340–410k packets/s on Windows and 620–870k on Linux.
- With Linux's default buffer, MTU 9000 at 1 Gbit/s dropped **7.2%**.
- Requesting 16 MiB with `SO_RCVBUF` was silently capped to 425,984 bytes. `SO_RCVBUFFORCE` got 32 MiB ([socket(7)](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/socket.7.html)).

**Against the fake camera:**
- With the capped buffer, kernel UDP receive-buffer errors rose by 641 in 3 s, and only 3 of 53 frames were complete, at just 50 Mbit/s. Each frame arrives as one burst and the tail gets dropped.
- With the forced 32 MiB buffer: 0 errors, 75/75 frames complete.
- Aravis's C receiver kept up with a buffer sized to one frame (the same cap); its fixed default buffer also dropped packets.

**`udp_multicam_threads_benchmark.py`, several cameras in one process:**
- N receiver threads, 1 Gbit/s per simulated camera.
- With the GIL, drops at MTU 1500 reached **39–75% at 4 cameras** and 77–88% at 8.
- The same Python 3.14.0rc3 free-threaded build with `-X gil=0` dropped **0% at 8 × 1 GbE** (679k packets/s, 1.39 cores). With `-X gil=1` it collapsed again.
- SkellyCam can already run one process per camera (`WorkerMode` in `managed_worker.py`).

**Buffer limits by OS:**
- macOS caps buffers at `kern.ipc.maxsockbuf`, default 8 MiB ([xnu socketvar.h L193](https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/xnu/blob/f6217f891ac0bb64f3d375211650a4c1ff8ca1ea/bsd/sys/socketvar.h#L193)).
- Windows' default was 64 KiB here. Vendors ship NDIS filter drivers (Windows only) to cut CPU load ([Basler docs](https://docs.baslerweb.com/pylon-software-suite)). A from-scratch client only gets the plain socket path.

## Options and effort (person-weeks)
